data.content:
Real Betis host Feyenoord in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday 21 October 2026, and the predicted lineups for both sides are shaped as much by who is missing as by who is in form. Betis must do without Junior Firpo, Cucho Hernández and the suspended Iker Losada, while Feyenoord go into this match missing two defenders, leaving selection questions at both ends ahead of kickoff. What follows sets out the expected XI for each side based on recent starting patterns, not any official team news. [...] | Player | Pos | Status | Reason |

| Junior Firpo | D | injured | Groin Injury |
| Iker Losada | F | suspended | Inactive |
| Cucho Hernández | F | injured | Calf Injury |

Thomas Beelen and Jordan Bos are out injured. Both are defenders, which leaves Feyenoord’s back line with less cover heading into this match. Sem Steijn and Thijs Kraaijeveld, the bench players with the most recent starts, stand out as the most obvious options to step in if required. [...] ## Injuries and Suspensions

Junior Firpo and Cucho Hernández are out injured, while Iker Losada is unavailable through suspension. With Firpo sidelined at full-back and Cucho Hernández also missing up front, this thins Betis’s options at both ends of the pitch ahead of kickoff. From the bench, Marc Bartra and Nelson Deossa – each with two starts across the matches used here – look the most likely to come into the side if changes are needed.

data.title: Real Betis vs Feyenoord Predictions, Picks & Odds - 21/10/2026
data.content: Real Betis hold a significant psychological advantage over Feyenoord, having already beaten the Dutch side 2-1 earlier this season in the Europa League. That result ended Feyenoord's European campaign, and the memory of that defeat will linger. Manuel Pellegrini's squad are well drilled and mentally sharp, with the veteran manager fostering a culture of focus and consistency throughout his seven-year tenure. [...] Feyenoord's form offers little encouragement for the visitors. A solitary defeat from their recent outings leaves them sitting in 33rd position in the league phase standings, a precarious spot that demands improvement. Travelling to Seville to face a confident Betis side brimming with momentum is far from an ideal fixture for a team struggling to find rhythm on the continental stage. [...] Real Betis head into this Champions League fixture at the Estadio La Cartuja de Sevilla in superb form, having won four of their last five matches with just a single draw breaking the sequence. Manuel Pellegrini's side sit twelfth in the league phase standings and carry genuine momentum. Their earlier victory over Feyenoord this season, a 2-1 triumph in January, provides both confidence and a tactical blueprint to lean on.
